**Test image observations:**
- Mango leaf with multiple small, circular discrete lesions scattered along the midrib
- Lesions have dark brown/black borders with lighter (necrotic) centers
- Some lesions show shot-hole appearance where the center has fallen out
- Green, otherwise healthy-looking leaf tissue

**Reference comparison:**
- Sooty_Mould shows a grayish-white to black sooty coating covering large leaf surface areas — does not match the discrete circular spots in the test image

**Reasoning:**
The discrete circular lesions with dark borders and lighter/necrotic centers on the mango leaf are characteristic of **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum gloeosporioides*), which causes small dark spots on mango leaves. Bacterial_Canker could produce shot-hole lesions, but Anthracnose is the primary cause of these discrete, dark, circular spots with necrotic centers on mango foliage. The pattern doesn't match Sooty_Mould (coating), Powdery_Mildew (white powder), Gall_Midge (galls/tubes), Cutting_Weevil (chewed edges), or Die_Back (tip/branch dieback).
